tagline: Farm country between the old mineral springs.
intro: Out of Peterstown the road takes Indian Creek's winding course first, then the gently rolling farm plateaus east of the county seat of Union, and finishes in the Sweet Springs Valley beside Peters Mountain. Industry largely passed this country by, so old houses, farms and public buildings from two centuries remain.

Stagecoach lines carrying settlers across the Alleghenies helped Union grow, and so did the mineral spring resorts within twenty-five miles of it, Sweet Springs, Red Sulphur Springs and Salt Sulphur Springs among them.

moments.title: Peterstown
moments.text: Named for pioneer settler Christian Peters, the town on the Virginia line is where a 34.48-carat diamond turned up in 1928.

moments.title: Indian Creek Covered Bridge
moments.text: Ray and Oscar Weikel built the 49-foot bridge in 1898; the county historical society owns it now, and it is open to pedestrians.

moments.title: Union
moments.text: The 1881 Romanesque courthouse stands among antebellum buildings from the years when the resort trade kept the local economy thriving.
